What it does

Not a prettier picture of you.
The garment, on your body.

These six map to the features in site.config.json — the website, the store listing and llms.txt all draw on the same copy.

01

Real 3D you can spin, not a rendered picture

A real-time 3D fitting room: turn to see the back, zoom into a cuff. Garment occlusion is computed geometry, not a guess.

02

Your real proportions, not a flattering edit

Height, body shape and facial features are a parametric human you shape yourself; garment fit is geometry.

03

Photograph a garment, and it joins your 3D wardrobe

Lay a real garment flat, take one photo: background removed, colour and pattern recovered, projected front and back.

04

No servers, no account

No cloud backend. Reconstruction, rendering and styling all happen locally; wardrobe and body data are never uploaded.

05

Scan your own bag into 3D (iPhone Pro)

Circle a small object with a LiDAR iPhone, rebuild it on device, then hang it on the avatar's hand or head.

06

A stylist that runs on your own API key

Optional AI styling advice: your provider, your bill. We do not resell inference.

“It doesn't flatter you. It tells you whether the garment fits.” How we decide what to build

Two different approaches

How this differs from photo-generation try-on

This is a comparison of engineering trade-offs, not a verdict. Photo generation can hand you a more flattering picture of yourself, and that is its strength. Below is what the other road buys you.

Dimension DressWell Photo-generation apps
What a try-on is Real-time 3D on device: spin, zoom, layer freely A cloud-generated 2D still; a new angle means generating again
Body A parametric human you shape; fit is computed geometry Generative models tend to render you slimmer, taller, more standard
Where data goes No servers, no account; wardrobe and body data stay on the phone Uploading face, full-body photos and your wardrobe is usually a prerequisite
AI cost Bring your own key, straight to your provider; we do not resell inference Subscription or per-use pricing with inference bundled in
Offline Fitting, avatar shaping and garment upload all work offline The core flow depends on online generation
Real objects A LiDAR iPhone can scan a small object on device and mount it Usually no counterpart

FAQ

Ask first, download second

These are also the FAQPage entries in the structured data — what you read here and what search engines read are the same text.

What is DressWell?

A 3D fitting room on your phone. You shape an avatar close to yourself — height, body, face, skin tone, hair — then style it with built-in garments or your own real clothes photographed into the app, and view it from any angle. Reconstruction, rendering and styling all run locally, and no account is required.

Are my photos and body measurements uploaded?

Not by default. DressWell has no servers and no account system: your avatar, saved looks and uploaded garments live in the app's own sandbox, with optional backup into your personal iCloud container. The one exception is if you deliberately configure your own model provider in Settings — the photo then goes directly to the endpoint you entered and is handled under that provider's retention policy. We never hold your key and never proxy the request, so we cannot see it either.

Does it work offline?

Yes. The fitting room, built-in garments, face and body shaping, and photographing your own clothes are all local computation and work in airplane mode. Only the optional AI styling advice needs a connection, because that step calls the model provider you configured yourself.

How much does it cost?

Free to download and genuinely usable: all built-in garments, hairstyles and hats are open, body and face shaping are unlimited, outfit changes come with a free allowance of 20, and you can keep 2 saved looks. Pro is a one-time purchase that lasts forever and unlocks unlimited outfit changes, unlimited saved looks, and photographing your own clothes. The stylist's paid skill packs are priced separately and are not included in Pro. No subscription, no ads.

Do I have to supply my own API key for the stylist?

Yes, and that is deliberate. You enter your own model provider in Settings — nine common ones come pre-filled — the request goes straight to that provider, and the bill is yours. That way we neither handle your photos nor need to fold inference costs into a subscription. Without a key the app still works, and everywhere AI would help falls back to doing it by hand.
